hero.caption: Logroño, 100-year storm: residential buildings at pluvial flood risk with present rainfall, and those newly at risk with future rainfall (90th percentile), by residents' social vulnerability

figures.caption: Future design rainfall increases residents in buildings at pluvial flood risk in Logroño
REACHOUT's planned nature-based solutions reduce residents at pluvial flood risk in Logroño by less than 4 %
City-wide greening takes mainly less socially vulnerable residents out of pluvial flood risk in Logroño

framing: Flood maps show where water goes. The risk framework of Vogelbacher et al. (2026), developed for Hamburg, also asks who lives there and how socially vulnerable they are. Applied building by building in Logroño, three signed studies find that today's 100-year storm becomes a 50- or 25-year storm, that the nature-based solutions planned so far, as modelled, offset little of this, and that greening all open space mainly protects the less vulnerable residents. The studies recommend placing measures first where the most vulnerable residents are at risk. Retold below for citizens and for schools.
headline: Heavier rain puts more of Logroño at flood risk, and the planned measures help little
